The six-person series documents baseline postural instability only. An isolated cold-pressed oil effect on clinical Parkinson postural instability remains unresolved.

Raw celery leaves contain butylphthalide, and human feeding studies show plasma apigenin. The pharmaceutical mouse report uses locomotion and coordination measures. A clinical butylphthalide registration planned Part IV motor complications and the likely matching conference report gives cognitive outcomes. Fresh celery leaf and clinical dyskinesia severity remain unresolved.

A Parkinson diet trial had a canola-containing low-fat menu and an inconclusive Part IV motor-complications comparison. The claim needs separately reported daily off time after cold-pressed canola exposure.

Dried leaf extract gave similar stool-day and constipation-score changes to placebo. Seed-oil data favor a selected score in athletes. The mixed-tablet patent evidence differs by formulation and one table contradicts its narrative. No result isolates whole fresh shiso for constipation in Parkinson disease. The direction remains unresolved.
Exploratory movement after ground whole hazelnuts in high-fat-fed mice lacks the toasted oil, Parkinson population and freezing frequency endpoint.
Macadamia kernel poisoning causes weakness and impaired movement in dogs. The oil, disease population and bradykinesia measure remain untested.

Clinical studies measured resting tremor during cabergoline treatment and described some improvement during a separate antibiotic interaction. Grapefruit juice raised drug levels in a small study that did not measure tremor. Fresh pulp was tested with other medicines. The shared meal, induced animal signs and public accounts do not establish a raw-grapefruit effect on resting tremor.

The safflower comparator in a PSP registration is oral and explicitly named. The protocol gives a motor composite and no separate walking-speed result. Existing exercise and ataxia walking trajectories differ. The claim remains open for cold-pressed oil in Parkinson disease.
A Parkinson diet plan used tarragon in two recipes. It does not specify dried state or report individual consumption. MDS-UPDRS III totals do not give a facial-expression item effect.

A mixed-oil patent gives a patient impression of swallowing the product. The texture-modified food study assesses healthy-volunteer chewing and bolus properties. These exposures leave cold-pressed canola effects on Parkinson swallowing unresolved.
A placebo-controlled sage-tip extract trial found no clear difference in dream recall. The report gives no dream enactment count or ground-sage Parkinson comparison.

The Parkinson diet menu lists walnut oil without grade, individual assignment or a rigidity-item result. Cold-pressed walnut oil improved climbing in a fly toxin model, which does not measure rigidity. The two records leave the clinical direction open.

Green cardamom powder has isolated digestive adverse-event reports outside Parkinson disease. An uncontrolled cardamom-containing mixture improved composite IBS severity. Another mixture trial prints selected bowel comments and supplies no arm prevalence or validated constipation severity. The direction for ground cardamom remains open.

Anise seed extract and fraction studies use animal memory and exploratory tasks with differing results and formulations. No clinical executive impairment result after ground seed in Parkinson disease was established.

Injected DHA lengthened strides in lesioned rats. In older adults without Parkinson disease, fish oil plus training versus olive oil plus training gave time-by-group p = .753 for single-task stride and .537 for dual-task stride. The roles of oral whole trout and grilling remain unresolved.

Concentrated tarragon essential oil impaired motor performance or produced ataxia in injected animal toxicity and seizure-model studies. An oral extract study measured general maze activity. These exposures and endpoints leave the direction of fresh tarragon on Parkinson postural instability unresolved.

One randomized non-Parkinson depression trial reports lower DASS-21 scores when nigella oil extract is added to sertraline versus sertraline alone (PMID35548175, 18.6 vs 23.4, p<.001, with a one-point arithmetic discrepancy in printed change). A ground-seed premenstrual trial favored a composite mood domain rather than depression severity (PMID41267796), while crushed-seed Bond-Lader mood (PMID24412554) and mixed-product depression trials in hypothyroidism (p=.79) and multiple sclerosis were inconclusive, and a hemodialysis trial has unreported HADS results. Oil preparation, co-treatment, reporting discrepancy, and absence of toasted-seed or Parkinson trials keep the easing lean at minimal_signal.

Both Baroni menus allowed potatoes and gave inconclusive ordinal OFF distributions. The Dresden study measured cold potato salad intake during medicated ON visits. Lunch reduced levodopa concentration variability during infusion without an identified potato exposure or daily OFF endpoint. The direction for roasted potato and daily OFF time remains unresolved.
Open-field activity did not change significantly in mice given injected extract. The fruit-drink trial measured exercise pain and did not time Parkinson walking.
The menu analysis reports total UPDRS III without an isolated dried lovage exposure or dyskinesia-severity change.

Boiled sweet potato with stew was tested in a run-based oxygen uptake study. A separate steamed sweet potato rice cake trial measured immediate cycling exertion and found no clear difference. Neither study measured fatigue severity in Parkinson disease.

A cooked-onion allergy case recorded acute dysphonia. The heated peel-extract trial uses about 1,000 mg active extract in 1,200 mg of capsules and reports a respiratory hoarseness item with baseline imbalance. Listener-rated speech after cooked onion in Parkinson disease remains unmeasured.

Two independent placebo-controlled menopause trials report less joint and muscular discomfort with oral Salvia officinalis fresh-tip extract (n=48 per-protocol of 80, p<.05) and dry extract (n=59, p<.001 with reversed table statistics), supported by a dose-comparison sage leaf throat-spray trial (n=164, p=.0021) and preclinical antinociception. Competing safety signals include one excessive-intake abdominal pain case (6/10) and a non-significant adverse-event count in an Alzheimer dry-extract trial (2 vs 0, p=.23), while perioperative/cancer rinse and mixed-herb trials give no isolated oral pain effect. Because no study evaluates fresh culinary sage or Parkinson pain severity, the controlled non-Parkinson discomfort reductions sustain only a minimal_signal against worsening.

A small wristband patent reports improvement with topical grapeseed oil, and a Parkinson rat study measured stride and grid descent after hydroalcoholic seed extract. Registered oral oil work concerns grip strength and has no posted result.

Different curry leaf extracts improved toxin-model movement initiation or worsened a drug-model catalepsy proxy. The 2012 extract result at 120 minutes was 110.0 seconds, and the 2025 administration route remains unverified. The diet pilot does not isolate ground curry leaf or report clinical bradykinesia by food.
Basil odor was misidentified by 74.3% in a Parkinson diagnostic study. The stimulus was smelled during an identification test and the study gives no olfactory change after eating basil.

The memory-care poster model gives a lower combined NPI score with topical and diffused almond oil than with lavender. It reports no visual hallucination counts. Oral cold-pressed almond oil and Parkinson hallucination frequency remain unresolved.

The closest tea consumption studies have no verified brewed-tea comparison against olfactory scores. Two Parkinson studies record tea and hyposmia separately, with their joint analysis and preparation unverified. Smell tests that present tea as an odor measure a different exposure. The clinical direction remains open.

In 97 people with Parkinson disease, gaining recognition of the coconut test odor was associated with worse standing lightheadedness scores (B = 1.147, nominal p = .003). The study used odor strips. The effect of consuming refined coconut oil remains unresolved.
A leaf-extract Parkinson model measured neuron histology and a separate leaf-oil seizure study reported motor impairment. Neither comparison measured stride length after culinary intake.

Parkinson depression trials used mineral or corn oil comparators. The blood fatty-acid preprint measures circulating levels and cannot identify intake. The refined-oil weight-loss trial still lacks accessible arm-level depression data. Evidence leaves the effect of isolated oral refined sunflower oil on Parkinson depressive symptoms unresolved.

Isolated oral capsaicin had divergent anxiety-like behavior findings in different rat models. A runner crossover shows an imprecise anxiety-event difference, and a human rocoto trial used another pepper species with insufficient group comparisons. Smoked paprika and clinical Parkinson anxiety remain untested.
Bay-leaf extracts and constituents affected gastric physiology in ethanol studies. No primary record measured levodopa exposure or daily OFF duration after ground leaf.

Mouse pole performance improved after red pepper decoction and a Parkinson case reported better walking while receiving combination treatment. Neither study counted freezing episodes after eating toasted Sichuan pepper.

Injected sesame oil increased rat anxiety-like behavior (PMID24409407), inhaled aroma studies test a non-oral route, and a Parkinson cannabinoid trial gave sesame oil to both arms (PMID38487964). The human oral comparison retains only a minimal_signal against worsening.

Depression was a secondary endpoint and the trial was powered for a biomarker. An independent Tehran trial favors saffron on Hamilton depression scores, with two other depression measures inconclusive and capsule processing unverified. The Shiraz non-Parkinson stigma adjunct comparison is inconclusive and the isolated crocin mouse result is indirect. The matched Parkinson comparison supports easing and therefore opposes the frozen worsening claim. Effects at ordinary meal quantities and independent replication with the same preparation remain open.

Examiner and daily-living Parkinson speech ratings showed no clear plasma ALA association. Neither speech intelligibility testing nor an isolated cold-pressed oil comparison was available.

Isolated eugenol studies in toxin models give timing-dependent motor outcomes and an inconclusive abnormal-behavior comparison with levodopa. These studies leave ground allspice and Parkinson dyskinesia severity open.

The urinary trial with extra-virgin oil as a comparator ended with no posted results. An unrelated saw-palmetto paper and registry disagree about their placebo. A randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled Parkinson trial of isolated caffeine capsules reports a 6-week UPDRS III bradykinesia subscore difference of -1.70 points (95% CI -3.10 to -0.31; limb-only CI crossed zero; PMID22855866), bridged to brewed black tea by infusion chromatography showing lower caffeine per cup (PMID40647065). Competing evidence includes an inconclusive longer-term caffeine total-motor trial (-0.48, 95% CI -3.21 to 2.25; PMID28954882), an observational PPMI preprint reporting faster progression (body unverified), non-replicated LRRK2 composite findings, and mixed rat exploratory activity. The direct Parkinson bradykinesia constituent RCT supports limited_clinical_link (51), matching claim 0904.
The Parkinson diet survey recorded cumin intake and anxiety measures. It did not isolate toasted cumin or a specific anxiety effect.

The RRIPP-3 macadamia comparator study found inconclusive between-group mood results. A terminated BRAVO registry contains a macadamia-oil comparison beverage and negative-affect outcomes without posted estimates. Neither study identifies a cold-pressed oil effect in Parkinson disease.

The isolated-eugenol mouse beam results differ across schedules that lack separately matched model controls. The other reports measure exploratory behavior, rotation or abnormal movement. Ground allspice and clinical Parkinson walking slowness remain unresolved.

The trial menus offer uncooked spinach or kale, with individual intake and listener-rated speech outcomes unreported. The original spinach search hit describes gardening advice in a communication interview.

Iron-biofortified versus conventional pearl millet increased light physical activity and had reported reaction-time findings in the same feeding program. Other work measured grip strength. These outcomes leave hand dexterity after cooked millet in Parkinson disease open.

A Parkinson self-experiment included ground white mustard in broccoli tea and described balance, with no recorded fall count or mustard-only comparison. Black mustard extract changed animal motor tests without a clinical fall-frequency measure.

Rosemary extract and isolated rosmarinic acid changed general movement in model mice. A seven-oil blend measured laboratory gait. No report isolates ground rosemary and walking slowness in people with Parkinson disease.

The recovered 1949 Parkinsonian series reports smaller tremor amplitude under drug treatment with unchanged incidence and frequency. Peanut oil was only an injected drug carrier, with no oil-only comparison. The separate oral oil studies address allergy, activity, metabolism or other outcomes. No signed result transfers to cold-pressed peanut oil and Parkinson resting tremor.

Human Sjögren salivary flow was measured with a corn oil comparator. Rat gland flow and topical corn-derived lubrication give separate outcomes. The available Parkinson carrier report gives a composite and leaves clinical drooling severity under dietary refined corn oil unresolved.
Curry leaf extract changed climbing, jumping and motor-task proxies in toxin models. Some other extracts prolonged catalepsy. Clinical freezing episodes after eating cooked leaf remain open.

The 1885 volume discusses almond oil for local respiratory application, while the 1936 oil hit was a separate injection vehicle. Those reports give no vocal intensity after oral cold-pressed almond oil. The 1897 case reports intralaryngeal almond oil as a menthol carrier, then other treatment and surgery before hoarseness resolved. The historical oral prescription gives no measured loudness or pressing grade.

Curry leaf extracts altered intestinal charcoal transit in opposite directions across models. The human iron-tablet study measured lower levodopa exposure. The curry leaf food studies measured iron or in vitro properties, with no levodopa or daily OFF-time comparison.

A randomized hospital nutrition package that included fortified oatmeal reduced observed falls. The group also received supplements and dietary counseling. No rolled oats contrast or separate Parkinson falls estimate was reported.

The Parkinson survey recorded cayenne intake but no ingredient-specific anxiety estimate. A controlled student thesis used a different Capsicum species and extract, with inconsistent anxiety table counts. Ground cayenne and Parkinson anxiety remain unresolved.

A meal crossover measuring supine pressure and a ground cassia beverage trial gave inconclusive acute contrasts. Other populations have mixed resting or ambulatory pressure results. Active-standing lightheadedness after ground cinnamon in Parkinson disease remains unmeasured.

The Parkinson cohort associates daytime sleepiness with whole diet scores. The boiled black bean crossover measures vascular and metabolic responses. The MIND daytime dysfunction contrast is inconclusive, and the soybean extract studies concern task-day or waking-time measures in healthy adults. The effect of boiled black common beans on Parkinson daytime sleepiness remains unresolved.

A topical piperine rinse series found improvement in a combined pronunciation and taste score in patients with burning-mouth syndrome. Parkinson speech intelligibility after eating ground black pepper remains unresolved.

Two open-label randomized trials outside Parkinson disease report lower state anxiety after solid dark chocolate versus no snack before thyroid biopsy (n=99, STAI group-by-time p=.01) or mineral water in trainee nurses (n=47, 3 days), leaving expectancy effects unresolved. No controlled evidence shows anxiety worsening; the non-Parkinson easing trials retain a minimal_signal against worsening.
Isolated lentinan improved some model behaviors. Shiitake extract experiments measured cells. No study tested hand dexterity after roasted shiitake in Parkinson's.
