A Parkinsonism survey included handwriting or typing and a grouped raw vegetable question. A direct uncooked pepper comparison measured temperature and autonomic outcomes in healthy adults. A raw sweet pepper and Parkinson handwriting-size comparison remains open.

The blinded healthy-volunteer leaf tea study gave no clear separation in sleep reports. Favorable inhaled oil findings had design limits. Isolated myrcene changed barbiturate-induced sleep under injection, oral and inhaled conditions, with opposite associations across acute and repeated oral schedules. The leaf-food comparison in Parkinson insomnia remains open.

Garden lovage appears in a multicomponent Parkinson menu without a dream-enactment result. Prospective diet-pattern work measures probable REM behavior disorder before diagnosis and does not isolate dried lovage or count episodes.
Turkey aroma chemistry characterizes the food and pooled poultry intake produced an inconclusive total symptom estimate. Neither assesses smell impairment after baked turkey.

Rodent tarragon preparations increased selected exploration, grooming or social measures. Sucrose preference was inconclusive, and a reported social-test p value conflicts with the printed statistic. Extracts and behavioral proxies give no directional estimate for dried culinary tarragon and Parkinson apathy.

Concentrated fruit extract impaired rotarod retention in healthy mice. Two Parkinson-model reports found improved performance under different extraction and exposure regimens. No study measured postural instability after toasted seeds in people with Parkinson’s.

Clinical imaging and diet cohorts assessed apathy without an isolated dried date comparison. The whole dry Ajwa crossover collected an unpublished mood diary, and the adjunct schizophrenia trial gives composite results. Date animal studies measured movement, nociception or reward-related proxies outside the frozen preparation and endpoint.

Both post-COVID groups received the same ungraded oral peanut oil and reported joint pain. Animal and topical comparisons use other routes. A dopamine nanoparticle experiment used peanut oil as a carrier and did not measure pain. Refined peanut oil and clinical Parkinson pain remain unresolved.

A liquid-meal study reported postural intolerance with presyncope. A separate lunch study found a smaller orthostatic pressure drop after eating. The reports do not isolate steamed brown rice or estimate orthostatic lightheadedness severity.

A cooked chervil soup allergy case describes acute airway and voice symptoms with no visual hallucinations. The Parkinson diet menu does not report hallucinations by herb. Poisoning cases involving other Apiaceae do not identify garden chervil.

The Parkinson whole-diet comparison aggregated motor complications and reported a ketogenic-arm dyskinesia case involving changes in medication. A separately measured severity effect from cold-pressed canola remains unresolved.
Estragole from another plant oil alters isolated skeletal-muscle contractile responses; it is not tarragon administration or patterned dystonia in a living Parkinson patient.

A 14-person red-perilla extract crossover found 0.24 fewer nighttime voids per night versus starch, with a very low baseline and an inconclusive daytime comparison. A separate oral perilla-extract study prolonged rat void intervals by 27%. Both experiments favor lower void frequency with their tested extracts. The frozen endpoint is the frequency of urgent episodes. Neither source measures urgency, fresh culinary shiso or the response in Parkinson disease.

The Tartary buckwheat sprout-powder preprint found an inconclusive primary cognitive result and mixed exploratory performance, including faster Flanker and Stroop responses and less improvement on one sustained-attention variability measure. It did not test toasted groats or Parkinson’s.

Parkinson constipation handout lists chervil among fiber-containing herbs, but supplies no consumption comparison, preparation-specific exposure or patient bowel outcomes. Chervil-soup allergy case describes acute throat and voice changes, not constipation.

Healthy adults assigned soy-oil capsules reported nearly unchanged sleep-quality scores after eight weeks. The only drowsiness complaint was in the lysolecithin arm. The registry postdates follow-up and lists no separate sleepiness endpoint. Oil refining and a Parkinson daytime sleepiness effect remain unresolved.
No directly matched directional human Parkinson's evidence qualified. Local lexical pairs: 3. External records screened: 11.

A paprika oleoresin trial in adults with mild knee pain found no clear pain-VAS or total JKOM contrast. A separate carotenoid trial lists adverse events in both groups and did not measure pain severity. The registered knee study has no reported results and its match to the paper is unverified.
A Parkinson diet trial analyzed an everyday motor aggregate that includes handwriting without giving the handwriting item or size. Independent cold-pressed canola effects remain unresolved.
Oral eugenol shortened narrow-beam crossing when given before toxin exposure and prolonged crossing after exposure in mice. Clinical fall frequency after ground clove remains untested.

The refined-oil DICe pilot favored sunflower over coconut for exploratory switching. MEMO and the Jenkins trial did not distinguish high-oleic sunflower from active comparators for executive change. Seed oil improved recognition memory in scopolamine-treated mice and students improved recall in a single-group study. Very high-fat sunflower and palm-kernel diets worsened radial-maze performance. A second rat study found more working-memory errors after a combined sunflower and saline regimen than in untreated controls. The handling difference limits oil attribution. The Parkinson clinical record measured a composite and the Parkinson models used a shared injected vehicle. No interpretable direction transfers to cold-pressed sunflower oil and a separate Parkinson executive outcome.

Oral comparator arms using peanut oil show some within-arm improvement in depression scores. These include healthy volunteers, irritable bowel syndrome and a vitamin D trial, all without an independent refined-oil comparison. The peanut-only arm of a topical and inhalational trial also improved. Planned diabetes program depression results are unavailable. These exposures and populations leave direction unresolved for refined peanut oil in Parkinson disease.

An individual case improved after powdered nutmeg in milk. The student infusion reports lack a usable between-group estimate or combine sleep education. A separate mace-aril study lacked a comparator, and the mixed-botanical trial was inconclusive across active arms. Parkinson insomnia remains open.

A Parkinson thesis used a multiingredient honey mixture containing anise seed. It reports no handwriting-size outcome tied to intake. Isolated anise oil and constituent studies used different motor measures.

UMIN000018516 reports no difference in hoarseness or itching after multiherb Hange-koboku-to versus no formula around intubation; no counts or loudness data and the tested brand or perilla content is not confirmed.

An older-adult trial of tulsi and cardamom extract did not publish a clear between-arm change in its accessible abstract. A Crohn trial measuring depression included cardamom in both groups. Ground cardamom and Parkinson depression remain unresolved.

Isolated beta-caryophyllene improved a mouse pole-task time, and eugenol had opposing movement patterns before and after MPTP. Injected essential oil studies add different animal motor proxies. The effects do not resolve the direction for culinary ground clove and clinical bradykinesia.

Black mustard seed extract improved general activity in drug-treated rats. The motor tests leave step and stride geometry unmeasured, while the toasted preparation and clinical Parkinson gait comparison remain open.
Oral avocado oil was associated with fewer rotations in a unilateral Huntington-like injury model. The publication family did not establish cold pressing or assess dystonic movements.

A ground sumac hypertension trial reported zero insomnia events versus one on placebo and an invalid printed p value. Historical sumac sleep use and unrelated seed-extract schedules add no comparative insomnia severity result. The sparse adverse-event data do not supply a direction.

The oral comparator gives no clear within-arm anxiety change and differs from roasted peanuts. Topical peanut carrier reports and a composite mouse oil substitution give no independent human oil contrast. The diabetes support trial reports only program-level anxiety. Cold-pressed peanut oil and clinical Parkinson anxiety remain unresolved.

The Parkinson cohort documents oregano use without an individual drooling result. Oral oil jelly measured pH, with drooling as the sample method. The effervescent dosage-form patent describes salivation without a clinical fresh-oregano comparison.

The dried-leaf infusion pilot reports Parkinson nonmotor totals with no separate attention estimate. Nasal oil studies measured EEG or stress and the mouse study measured memory after injected extract. None measured attention impairment after eating fresh marjoram.

A Parkinson diet pilot listed pumpkin seed oil and included rigidity in a composite score without giving separate effects. In one rotenone mouse experiment, seed extract shortened bar-test immobility late and prolonged it at a lower dose earlier. Toasted oil and clinical rigidity remain open.
Parkinson inpatient mixed vegetarian menu listed parsley; UPDRS III total improved but individual herb intake, drying and stride-length changes were not reported.

The original allspice oil abstract reports oral irritation and sedation in rats. A related speech-loss case involved a different clove oil and alcohol. Neither measures human speech intelligibility or clinical change after ground allspice.

The oral clove study's anxiety-labelled table corresponds to Beck depression methods and has no separate anxiety test. A Parkinson multi-odor trial reports anxiety changes but did not isolate eugenol or ground clove. The frozen direction remains unresolved.

Oral common chive leaf extract in stroke-model mice had neurological and Morris water-maze outcomes; abstract contains no anxiety result. Ferulic acid studies are isolated constituent rather than dried chives.
A model tested isolated lentinan and surveillance recorded skin reactions to raw or undercooked shiitake. Neither assessed clinical postural instability after cooked shiitake.
Parsley appeared in a mixed Parkinson diet menu; no assigned fresh-leaf exposure or separate hand dexterity or finger-tapping item results appear.

The marjoram tea pilot measured composite nonmotor and depression scores. The Tlemcen mixture thesis lists sleep disturbance across the survey. Separate insomnia severity after consuming dried marjoram remains unresolved.

A fetal study and its neonatal follow-up examined facial behavior around kale flavor exposure. Roasted kale laboratory work measured aroma and a sensory rehabilitation study listed kale as optional. None isolates eating roasted kale against clinical olfactory impairment in Parkinson disease.

A Parkinson whole-diet comparison used boiled potato in mixed meals and did not isolate its effect on sleepiness. A pediatric mash crossover registered acute sleepiness and the probable linked abstract omits that outcome. Frying and baking protocols measure related symptoms with no boiled-potato result.

A Parkinson diagnostic test used dried sage as an odor. A separate common-sage oil aromatherapy study required intact smell and measured satisfaction. The effect of consuming ground sage on clinical olfaction remains unknown.

Brewed lemongrass evidence covers recalled dreams and nightmares outside Parkinson disease. Aroma and topical studies cover global sleep or distressing dreams. Injected oil studies measure drug-induced sleep, a postpartum mixed drink measures reported hours, and a flavored placebo trial records a nightmare separately from sleep efficiency. None provides witnessed dream enactment or REM without atonia after brewed lemongrass in Parkinson disease.

Both Parkinson diet menus permit kale or spinach and individual choices are unverified. The urinary item difference compares complete diets. The processed-seed registry has no posted results. The raw-kale urgency-frequency direction remains unresolved.

In 19 healthy trained men a seven-day 3 g/day commercial cayenne capsule crossover found no between-treatment difference in fastest or mean 30-m sprint time; gastrointestinal symptom score was 6.3 times higher. Sprint speed and capsule are not everyday walking or a Parkinson trial. Existing chili FFQ study reports composite sarcopenia without a chili-specific walking contrast.

A whole Parkinson diet menu includes lovage without identifying drying or apathy by lovage exposure. Individual apathy was measured in a different dietary-pattern survey without a lovage estimate. Root extract and other botanicals called lovage do not establish direction for dried garden lovage leaves.

An extract of the dried whole celery plant altered beam and drag behavior in mice. Neither those motor proxies nor related constituents estimate dystonia after fresh culinary celery leaf in Parkinson disease.

An open-label Parkinson study reported no clear change in constipation severity or bowel frequency after a multicomponent bar containing rice bran. The effect of refined rice bran oil remains unresolved.

Oral alcoholic allspice leaf extract produced sedation and motor incoordination in animal toxicity observations. An essential-oil study also reported sedation, without a handwriting task. Ground allspice and Parkinson micrographia remain unresolved.
Morris water-maze and neurological severity outcomes after oral common chive extract in ischemic mice do not supply a clinical executive-function contrast or fresh chive ingestion effect.

The tauopathy mouse study measured REM without atonia and used peanut oil as the drug comparator vehicle. The independent Alzheimer-model study tested a drug and REM stage duration. Neither supplies dream-enactment frequency after cold-pressed oil.

Formulated oral curcumin gave a favorable Trail A result, an adjustment-sensitive acute vigilance difference and imprecise Yale attention change. Other controlled Flanker and cognitive-battery comparisons gave inconclusive differences. The Parkinson studies do not release a separate attention result. The findings leave the effect of grated turmeric on Parkinson attention unresolved.

Injected haloperidol nanocapsules with grapeseed oil changed vacuous chewing in rats. The movement endpoint, drug exposure and route cannot determine oral cold-pressed oil’s effect on Parkinson dystonia.

Eugenol prolonged barbiturate-induced loss of righting in rats. Post-deprivation behavior under a nanoemulsion and an allspice chemistry review do not measure natural insomnia after ground culinary allspice.

A randomized plant-rich Parkinson diet study observed no clear change in Epworth daytime sleepiness and gives no raw-carrot exposure. General-population blood carotenoid associations vary in direction, with no raw-carrot-specific result.

Injected allspice leaf extracts suppressed CNS activity in rats. The original study did not measure mood. Isolated eugenol experiments give favorable and inconclusive behavioral signals with different formulations. Ground allspice berry and Parkinson depressive severity remain unmeasured.

Two trials favored a coated proprietary cantaloupe concentrate on some fatigue outcomes. Other melon preparations had inconclusive fatigue results. Protective coating changes the tested formulation. The evidence leaves fatigue after eating raw cantaloupe in Parkinson disease unresolved.

The Parkinson study compared a strain-specific fermented milk with acidified milk and reported only total motor scores. Its table supplies within-arm analyses with no separate hand dexterity result or between-arm motor estimate. The product is not identified as plain kefir.

An unblinded primary-dysmenorrhea trial reports larger VAS pain reduction when whole turmeric powder is added to naproxen (7.0 vs 5.6, p<.001), but has an unresolved design and sample discrepancy versus its registry (149 parallel vs 90 crossover) and an implausible spread value. A double-blind hand-osteoarthritis pilot of whole turmeric powder (n=27) was inconclusive on primary one-month and between-group comparisons at all visits despite favorable three-month within-arm changes, and formulated-extract or black-pepper-addition trials gave null primary between-arm pain contrasts. Isolated curcumin rodent assays and mixed-formula or survey accounts do not isolate culinary ground turmeric in Parkinson disease; the whole-powder add-on trial sustains only a minimal_signal easing lean.
A whole walnut snack had inconclusive short-term salivary-flow results. The study gives no clinical drooling estimate, cold-pressed oil exposure or Parkinson sample.

One randomized non-Parkinson menopause trial reports lower one-month insomnia scores with sweet-basil (Ocimum basilicum) leaf extract versus placebo (IRCT20200104046001N1, n=60, 5.6 vs 11.0, p<.001). An independent triple-blind postpartum trial of dried sweet-basil leaf powder versus placebo found no clear total sleep-quality difference (IRCT20220926056046N2, 17.63 vs 16.15, adjusted p=.400), and injected isolated myrcene assays in mice measured barbiturate-induced sleep with opposite acute versus repeated timing effects. Absence of fresh culinary basil and Parkinson insomnia trials plus the null postpartum trial keep the easing lean at minimal_signal.

Two closely related bay-odor reports found better late visual vigilance at the lower odor load in healthy men. The earlier 11-person comparison reported p=.026 across 30 minutes and the later nine-person comparison recorded 93.8% versus 88.0% at 30 minutes. The high odor load showed no clear accuracy benefit and the samples may overlap. The exposure was inhaled; effects of eating ground bay leaf on Parkinson attention remain open.

Nigella oil rinse improved early normal-diet tolerance during mucositis, with an inconclusive day-28 comparison. Reflux registration specifies nigella-derived melanin and a GERD score. Neither isolates eating ground nigella or measures Parkinson swallowing impairment.

Self-selected Parkinson records use ground white mustard alongside broccoli seed in mixed tea; the available selected self-rated symptom records do not report a visual-hallucination-frequency comparison or isolate mustard. Spontaneous patient symptom selection and simultaneous other ingredients prevent inference.
No directly matched directional human Parkinson's evidence qualified. Local lexical pairs: 0. External records screened: 0.

Fresh green kiwi yielded an imprecise change in self-rated waking alertness. The controlled breakfast study gives inconclusive choice reaction-time and Stroop results after previously frozen kiwi pulp, and the separate COMPASS registry lacks results. The new kiwi meal experiment measured pig brain bioamines. These outcomes leave the direction for raw kiwi and Parkinson attention impairment unresolved.

Some allergic children had hoarseness during ground roasted hazelnut challenges. Edible oil intake, vocal loudness, and Parkinson hypophonia were not established. A separate pooled pediatric report also uses a different voice and throat outcome.

The 12-week Longvida trial found less worsening on a combined PSQI daytime dysfunction component. Few improved in either arm, and no separate sleepiness item was given. Epworth was inconclusive in another formulated trial and was unreported in the Parkinson nanomicelle study. No directional result was found for eating grated turmeric and daytime sleepiness.

2014 crossover in ten trained men, nine with exercise data, combined aqueous Russian tarragon extract or placebo with creatine in both arms; sprint peak power, mean power and total work interactions p=.92, .27 and .27. These are performance tests rather than clinical fatigue after dried culinary leaves.

Canine corn-oil diets give comparator-sensitive detection results without established refining grade. Other studies use injections, an odor-pen solvent or oil preference after induced smell loss. These exposures do not resolve the direction for ingested refined oil in Parkinson disease.

The Parkinson diet trial supplies only total motor scores. Heated oil carrying mung bean extract and Cucurbita extract studies use rodent suspension or rotarod tasks. No source isolates cold-pressed pumpkin seed oil and manual dexterity.
Among 126 adults 31.0% identified dried marjoram odor; stimulus recognition is not a treatment effect on olfactory impairment after eating marjoram.

Unspecified dill tablets and a topical preparation improved questionnaire totals in other clinical settings. The tablet source does not identify plant part or insomnia subitems. The topical baseline has a reporting conflict, and the completed extract-beverage trial has no public results. Injected mouse locomotion does not measure sleep. The dried leaf and Parkinson insomnia comparison remains open.

Exercise with inhaled Zanthoxylum limonella oil improved selected eyes-closed sway measures versus almond scent. Reach and fear-of-falling interactions were inconclusive. Related Japanese pepper improved a rodent coordination measure. Neither tests ground Sichuan pepper and Parkinson postural instability.

The essential voice tremor crossover used soybean oil of unspecified grade as placebo and measured sustained vowel amplitude modulation. It gives no isolated refined oil estimate or measure of habitual Parkinson voice volume.

Related isolated cineole or non-cardamom leaf oil experimental motor studies examine induced rodent catalepsy, with different formulations and models; opposing model outcomes cannot be reclassified as dystonia. The cardamom spice review does not supply clinical item-level dystonia data.

The Parkinson powder trial gives no posted voice-volume outcomes and diet menus do not verify individual frozen berry intake. In a separate case, hoarseness progressed after blueberry avoidance and imaging identified an anatomical cause. No study supplies a frozen-blueberry vocal-volume estimate in Parkinson disease.

Intracerebral isolated green-leaf chalcone in 6-OHDA mice improved aggregate behavior; no clinical rigidity or fresh-leaf ingestion. Separate 2024 rotenone mouse perilla seed-oil study improved pole descent, a motor-speed task, and did not measure rigidity.
No directly matched directional human Parkinson's evidence qualified. Local lexical pairs: 1. External records screened: 2.

Mixed menus and the high-fiber pilot provide aggregate motor outcomes. Studies using apple as a movement, eating or chewing task measure oral function or motor characteristics. The 2025 and 2023 chewing reports share one cohort. No isolated raw-apple effect on resting-tremor severity was measured in these comparisons.

All 60 allergy-trial participants tolerated the refined oil challenge. Pediatric reports list pooled hoarseness and separate labial oil challenges without oil-specific voice change. The acute allergy outcomes leave habitual Parkinson voice volume unresolved.
Both diet menus in a Parkinson randomized trial list cooked thyme of unspecified freshness. The more favorable composite Part I result cannot isolate thyme or the apathy item.

An extract trial in healthy adults found faster acute attention and fewer false alarms alongside worse name-to-face accuracy. Healthy gamer registrations provide no results, and clinical Parkinson’s attention after toasted pepper remains unresolved.

Culinary asparagus stem extract studies give within-period or uncontrolled fatigue results. A comparison of a different species and root extract improved perimenopausal fatigue at week eight, with no clear effect at week four. Roasted shoots and clinical Parkinson fatigue remain unresolved.

No controlled study isolates virgin coconut oil for apathy severity. The Parkinson baseline figure (MVP-2024) plots only an unquantified tile for motivation/initiative without oil grade, adjustment, or error limits. The Parkinson ketogenic MCT feeding study (PMID38561682) found no clear between-group diary apathy difference without isolating virgin coconut oil, and KIM (NCT05469997) reported no post-diet apathy comparison. The claim therefore moves from legacy 51 to open.
The oral sage extract study measured paw-print function after peripheral nerve injury. It supplies no evidence of clinical fall frequency after ground sage.

Parkinson trial assigned encapsulated dried common sage or vitamin E for six weeks, but accessible outcome attachment reports cognition and salivation without handwriting or a timed hand-task estimate; fresh leaves differ.

Two independent urinary infection cohorts reported lower symptom scores after a lovage-root, rosemary and centaury product. One is uncontrolled and the other compares the blend with fosfomycin. The available urgency results concern symptom severity, and neither cohort measured episodes after dried lovage leaf in Parkinson disease.

A mouse study reported longer drug-induced sleep after oregano infusion. A healthy-volunteer crossover found no apparent change in overnight sleep architecture with oregano extract. Neither measured daytime sleepiness after dried oregano in Parkinson’s.

A human metabolic syndrome trial found no clear blood-pressure difference between avocado and soybean oils. Rat studies report lower pressure in hypertensive animals, with no clear change in normotensive rats. Refined oil and Parkinson orthostatic symptoms remain open.

Four PD cases received sequential lemongrass-oil inhalation and massage; clear-writing difficulty ratings remained 0, 0, 1 and 1 across phases. Questionnaire does not measure letter size, oil is nonoral and botanical species not established.

Bok choy appears in a grouped Taiwanese falls questionnaire with no separate cooked ingredient result. A controlled steamed bok choy meal measured glucose. No study linked cooked bok choy to Parkinson postural instability.

Phillips 2018 ketogenic and low-fat diets list thyme as a seasoning, with cooked dishes and unspecified species/freshness. UPDRS II total contains handwriting but no item-level estimates, ingredient intake or isolated thyme contrast.

A ground anise seed comparison assessed dyspepsia rather than hand response. Essential oil changed mouse rotarod performance under midazolam challenge. Neither identifies manual dexterity after culinary ground anise in Parkinson disease.
Chamuangone-enriched rice bran oil improved rat stride length in a haloperidol comparison. The design did not include plain refined rice bran oil or clinical Parkinson stride outcomes.
A cod hydrolysate trial in older adults found inconclusive grip effects. No study tested grilled cod against Parkinson micrographia.

Two Parkinson mixed menus mention cucumber without a separate posture effect. Exact source bodies yield sea cucumber and unrelated gait or diagnostic matches. The lead-exposure rat extract paper gives no accessible assay name or arm estimates and cannot resolve effects of raw cucumber.

A labor analgesia study compared epidural selection while both groups ate millet porridge. Poisoning cases involved pesticide-contaminated flour. Neither provides a clean boiled millet comparison for Parkinson pain.

Randomized older-women trial used powdered ginger in water; hypertensive SBP changed 145.82→142.54 mmHg on ginger versus 150.00→147.30 on control, similar changes. It measures resting pressure, no standing challenge or lightheadedness; grating and Parkinson status do not match. In an independent 22-man meal study, ginger was finely chopped and serial BP was measured; standing symptom was not assessed.

Grapefruit juice changed measured cabergoline concentration in a five-person Parkinson study. The tendon study used locally applied vesicles in mice. The separate original conference presentations provide no raw grapefruit stride comparison.

A Parkinson diet listed oregano, but reported medication-dose changes and no daily OFF duration, with differing figures in its narrative and table. A marjoram tea study used another species and a motor total. The oregano enzyme assay did not measure clinical OFF time.
Sumac extract was tested in Parkinson-derived cells and separate model experiments use other species or compounds. No comparison measured muscle rigidity after ground culinary sumac.

Rat offspring receiving interesterified fat showed less adult locomotion than the soybean oil comparator under a developmental protocol. Refined oil grade and clinical bradykinesia effects remain unresolved.

Parkinson Sargol powder tablet study planned MDS-UPDRS Part II, which includes item 2.2 saliva/drooling; an item assessment or total cannot establish a measured item-specific effect. Related 8-week saffron trial abstract reports MDS-UPDRS I item 3 and Part III rather than drooling.

An author abstract reports a larger dysarthria score change after adding an egg-yolk-derived oil to standard care in people with hemiplegia. The administration route and individual speech measures await the original. A poached-egg speech intelligibility effect in Parkinson disease remains unresolved.

Whole walnut studies showed task-dependent fall latency in rats, null rotarod results in aged mice and favorable dual-task postural sway in healthy older men. Human fall counts after cold-pressed walnut oil remain unresolved.

One placebo-controlled trial reports lower Hamilton anxiety scores with grape fruit extract in healthy older adults with low baseline anxiety (PMID29163162). Competing evidence includes an inconclusive 12-week whole-grape powder trial in postmenopausal women (PMC7257957, n=32 completers, numeric contrast omitted), mixed rotenone-rat behavioral proxies with dried Corinthian currants (open-field thigmotaxis p=.006 vs elevated-plus-maze p=.929), a null A53T mouse concentrate test, an order-affected acute juice study, and a pending college-student Hamilton trial (NCT07214428). No clinical trial tests raw grapes or Parkinson anxiety; the older-adult extract trial sustains a minimal_signal against worsening.

Enriched or extracted rice bran oil improved some rat coordination tasks. A historical contaminated oil exposure is not a culinary intervention. The selected original sources did not measure clinical hand dexterity after ingesting refined rice bran oil.

The Alzheimer comparator trial reports an apathy item but leaves a randomized contrast inconclusive. The Parkinson corn-vehicle trial gives only a part I composite. The proposed Parkinson apathy reduction remains undetermined.

Dried identified dill leaf capsules versus starch in 42 adults with diabetes: any esophageal complaint 3/21 to 5/21 versus 5/21 to 5/21; no drooling or salivary-flow measurement and no Parkinson subgroup.
The Parkinson prebiotic pilot listed green beans among several menu options. Its report and registry provide neither a fall count nor individual cooked bean intake.

Curry-leaf extracts tested in drug-induced rodent involuntary chewing and tongue movements, which are distinct from reduced facial expressivity; cooked whole leaves and patient item 3.2 were not tested.

A Parkinson trial used rice bran oil as a placebo and reported aggregate motor changes. Separate poisoning and odor studies include hoarseness or wet voice after swallowing. No study gives low voice volume after ingesting refined rice bran oil.

A Parkinson diet included millet in a multiingredient menu. Preparation, participant intake and follow-up dyskinesia severity were unavailable. The reported motor total cannot establish a millet effect.

Separate multiscent programs incorporating ginger found an inconclusive randomized TDI comparison and a favorable nonrandomized identification result. Both used olfactory training. Parkinson ginger-odor threshold testing also does not estimate a treatment effect of eating grated ginger.

Mixed Parkinson vegetarian diet listed lovage as seasoning, but exposure form and individual intake were unspecified and freezing episodes were not reported; total motor score does not resolve the leaf's effect.

A Parkinson diet menu includes parsley without a dyskinesia-specific comparison. Human dried leaf kinetics and motor testing of isolated apigenin in a model leave levodopa-induced dyskinesia after dried parsley unresolved.

2016 randomized 24-person trial reports within-tarragon systolic pressure 120.0 to 113.0 mmHg over 90 days; abstract lacks controlled change and standing symptoms, and uses a Russian tarragon supplement rather than fresh leaf.

Cold-pressed oil studies use animal recognition tasks. A mixed ketogenic case lists avocado-oil mayonnaise with narrative executive change. Whole fruit and mixed menus have registered outcomes with no available executive estimate for the matched Preiss report. The data cannot assign a direction to the oil claim.

Flaxseed table oil has a small healthy-adult fluency difference and an inconclusive total frontal battery. A pooled omega-3 cohort has faster global cognitive decline without a separate oil estimate. A new executive-composite registry has no results. These measures and exposures leave the frozen comparison unresolved.

No controlled trial shows that eating poached trout affects depressive symptom severity. The only randomized trout feeding trial (JGG2017-SHAPOURI-113, n=96 older adults) found a null adjusted GDS-15 difference (-0.17, 95% CI -0.48 to 0.15, p=.295) without specifying poaching or Parkinson disease. Angina fatty-fish advice had an interval crossing zero, and marine omega-3 supplement evidence is contradictory across small unspecified-species Parkinson pilots and VITAL-DEP (PMID34932079, higher incident depression with null mean PHQ-8). The claim therefore moves from legacy 51 to open.

In an uncontrolled Parkinson study, 13 of 14 participants who tracked urgency reported initial improvement with broccoli and ground white mustard tea. Some later reported transient worsening or fading benefit. The contribution of ground mustard by itself remains open.

Freeze-dried blackberry powder has a favorable reported fluid composite with unspecified contrast, and no significant virtual-maze flexibility effect. The thawed four-berry drink gives a switching interaction without a clear main effect. Neither establishes the direction for frozen blackberry alone in Parkinson disease.
Same 2021 marjoram infusion Parkinson trial reports motor and nonmotor totals but no identified dystonia episode or severity measure; no effect of fresh leaves can be isolated.

One randomized non-Parkinson trial reports higher stool frequency (p=.0281) and softer stools (p=.04) with added orange pomace versus control, alongside increased gas/bloating and an unavailable separate constipation severity score (NCT02979496). Competing evidence includes a null pomace crossover for primary stool-frequency interaction (PMID36102329, p=.46), sequential null pasteurized orange juice (PMID30638420), an unadjusted older-adult survey (p=.054), uncontrolled multi-component Chagas and trifoliate-orange studies, and a Fox Insight pooled-fruit binary bowel category pointing opposite. No trial tests raw whole orange in Parkinson constipation; the pomace stool-frequency trial retains a minimal_signal against worsening.

A small paprika xanthophyll study favored lower post-exercise fatigue. Separate capsule registrations leave participant fatigue open. The capsinoid cycling comparison supplies metabolic findings and leaves patient-rated fatigue open. Direction for raw bell pepper and Parkinson fatigue remains unresolved.

Dietary cold-pressed walnut oil improved climbing in a toxin-exposed fly study. A Parkinson diet menu contains walnut oil but gives only aggregate motor scores. Neither supplies a human oil-specific bradykinesia estimate.

A grape-seed extract reduced scored stiffness in a Parkinson-model rat experiment. A separate juice study measured turning, and the human Parkinson juice study recorded motor scores at baseline only. None establishes a rigidity direction for frozen whole grapes.

Closest PD signal: observational MVP self-reported coconut-oil use/frequency associated with lower composite PRO-PD symptom scores in overlapping cohorts; no urinary-urgency/frequency-specific coefficient and no virgin-grade confirmation. Separate MS pilot combined 60 mL coconut oil with EGCG and measured anxiety/function/IL-6, not urinary urgency. No defensible direction for urinary urgency/frequency. Open: identify any oil-specific urinary questionnaire item/analysis in the MVP source tables and any human protocol/results with urinary urgency as endpoint; do not infer from composite score.

One placebo-controlled menopause trial of fresh Salvia officinalis tip extract reports lower secondary POMS fatigue (PMID33615001, p=.029, without an arm-by-time fatigue table; separate sleep-exhaustion item unchanged). A dry-extract menopause trial gave an inconclusive exhaustion contrast (IRCT2015111713940N2, p=.634), Spanish-sage essential oil reduced acute healthy task fatigue (different species), Newcastle PD sage trial omitted fatigue, and a single multi-exposure FAERS report cannot attribute fatigue to sage. Extract transfer and multiplicity keep the lean against worsening at minimal_signal.
Cardamom is listed in a multicomponent Parkinson diet; reported total motor scores cannot establish a rest-tremor item response or cardamom attribution.
Infant poisoning involved green anise and star anise in a mixed infusion with neurological symptoms; seed identity, age, dose, coexposure and outcome differ from target.

The baseline Parkinson graphic gives a weak inverse sign for an unspecified coconut-oil category and a self-rated REM behavior item. It gives no episode count. The qualitative diet report describes dream behaviors and possible coconut or avocado oil use in different participants. Virgin oil and change in dream-enactment frequency remain unresolved.

The dried-thyme trial measures self-rated memory. Isolated thymol experiments report animal behavioral comparisons, and thyme oil studies report experimental cholinergic signaling. The direction of fresh thyme and clinical attention in Parkinson disease remains open.

Pinto-specific comparisons group different stool changes without a separate signed constipation severity result. The cooked bean rotation including pinto gave more frequent and softer stools than rice, but pooled bean types and measured no clinical constipation severity. The isolated Parkinson comparison remains unresolved.

Three oral ground Cinnamomum verum experiments from one research program report improved rotarod, open-field movement, and shorter timed pole turning/descent in aged A53T (PMID32889602, n=5-6/group; 2025 correction replaced separate benzoate histology panels) and MPTP mouse Parkinson models (PMID24946862, PMID31119595). No human clinical gait-speed trial isolates ground cinnamon (Park 2026 OA15.04 reports intake behavior only). Same-program mouse agility proxies without clinical gait data sustain only a minimal_signal against worsening.

Two other-oil or active-product comparisons in osteoarthritis supply no clear pain difference or oil-only estimate. A Mediterranean arthritis program reports less pain while changing many foods. The Sunola trial has an unresolved oil identity. Clinical Parkinson pain under cold-pressed canola remains unresolved.

Sensory and composition studies compare thawed, steamed or microwaved Brussels sprouts and their odor characteristics. They measure product smell or liking and do not estimate olfactory impairment after eating roasted sprouts.

An oral avocado comparator was used in repeat timed symbol transcription. The task counts symbols, and the study supplies no character-size measurements, refined-oil verification or Parkinson participants.

Two healthy-adult odor experiments found higher saliva secretion after pepper oil. One mixed whole-pepper and capsaicin care case reported increased drooling with inseparable exposures. Clinical drooling depends on saliva clearance as well as secretion. The available studies give no defensible direction for eating cracked pepper in Parkinson disease.

A Parkinson bundled menu lists spinach with no preparation or facial-expression item result. Aged-rat conditioned eyeblink learning and a separate conference abstract about preferred omelets do not measure Parkinson facial expressiveness.
Mixed Parkinson vegetarian menu lists chervil without plant dose or fresh preparation; total UPDRS III is not an individual rigidity result.

Pooled fish has a favorable association with a composite overactive bladder outcome outside Parkinson disease. The Parkinson study groups oily fish and urinary items. It supplies no grilled-sardine urgency frequency estimate.

The KIM trial phases encouraged unspecified olive oil and its insomnia event concerned an overall diet. A cannabis series recorded a within-dose insomnia change with shared ungraded olive oil. AU-ARROW plans the Insomnia Severity Index within a multidomain program using extra-virgin oil. A Parkinson insomnia effect specific to the oil remains open.

Oat bran served as a trial comparator with planned cognitive testing, and green oat extract affected cursor tracking in healthy adults. An enriched meal package containing oatmeal reported falls. Those outcomes leave isolated cooked oats and manual dexterity in Parkinson disease unresolved.

The age-adjusted plasma ALA correlation favored less rigidity, with a weaker sex-adjusted result. A combined-regimen narrative described improvement. The two flaxseed omega-3 plus vitamin E trials give aggregate results and omit a separate rigidity estimate. The first trial’s registry changed dose and outcomes after publication. No contrast isolates cold-pressed flaxseed oil.

The baked eggplant case identifies an acute allergy, with no dystonic reaction described. A separate cell experiment measures survival and oxidative markers under rotenone. The inherited clinical book review remains open at original depth and neither verified source links roasted eggplant to Parkinson dystonia.

The Korean survey estimates carrot frequency versus rhinitis and rhinitis versus smell loss in different models. Its printed carrot ratio and interval conflict. Raw-carrot aroma profiling and Parkinson smell testing do not give a raw-carrot intake effect.
Coriander seed-oil mouthrinse study measured salivary microbiome rather than flow or drooling; it is a rinse, not eaten dried leaf.

Three official protocols use protein blends or a pea beverage and include gait testing, with no posted results. Isolated pea lectin with paraquat affected forced forelimb behavior in rats. The walking effect of cooked green peas in Parkinson remains unresolved.

Isolated caffeine favored less Parkinson rest tremor at weeks three and six with intervals spanning zero. The trial used higher amounts than measured servings of black tea. Separate sources include worsening in some caffeine or coffee users, an acute oral caffeine test without clear worsening and tea cohorts with inconclusive or conflicting composite outcomes. The constituent link gives a minimal favorable lean for brewed black tea.
Mixed Parkinson vegetarian intervention lists chervil as seasoning but gives no individual intake, dried form, or herb-specific fatigue outcome; UPDRS III total does not measure fatigue.

The dried-leaf Parkinson pilot reports cognition and salivation without an apathy result. In healthy adults, the controlled dried-leaf comparison gave higher alertness before the stress task and lower task-associated alertness after the same dose. A probable mixed-sage trial family gives no clear mood contrast. Compound studies describe movement in animals, and a Parkinson effort task uses apathy as a participant characteristic. These outcomes do not establish a directional effect on clinical apathy from dried sage. The pilot's secondary timetable and the original constituent study tables remain open.
No directly matched directional human Parkinson's evidence qualified. Local lexical pairs: 36. External records screened: 40.
Capsaicin altered rat general motor activity under pharmacological conditions; this is neither measured Parkinson walking slowness nor smoked paprika ingestion.

The author abstract reports fewer abnormal involuntary movements after injected isolated capsaicin in lesioned rats. It leaves the levodopa regimen and scoring protocol unverified. A separate study found lower spontaneous and drug-elicited movement, making general activity suppression a competing explanation. Ground paprika capsaicinoid content varies, and no Parkinson dyskinesia direction can be assigned to oral ground paprika.

The rat Parkinson-like experiment used oral almond oil across all matched groups. Cardiovascular measures supply neither an oil-free contrast nor a standing symptom estimate. The processing grade is unverified.

The mixed Parkinson diet included thyme and reported nonmotor totals. It gives no thyme-specific effect on visual hallucination frequency. Other screened bodies measure distinct symptoms or exposures.

The clinical powder trial lists a composite motor scale with no posted separate speech result. Uncooked blueberry is an option on mixed menus, and a corticobasal case has no timed berry contrast. Raw blueberry and listener intelligibility remain unresolved.

No controlled or statistically clear evidence links cold-pressed flaxseed oil to bradykinesia severity. In early Parkinson disease (PMID34127758), plasma alpha-linolenic acid was non-significantly correlated with examiner-rated body bradykinesia (age-adjusted p=.171, sex-adjusted p=.372) and did not track dietary intake. Flaxseed omega-3 plus vitamin E trials (PMID28342967, PMID30554092) combined vitamin E, lacked isolated bradykinesia items, and reported inconclusive UPDRS Part III, while older-adult FAB motor series (p=.140) and rat activity (p=.595) were null and isolated-ALA animal tasks do not transfer. The claim therefore moves from legacy 51 to open.
A Parkinson diet offered whole hazelnuts among other ingredients and reported the total motor examination. The facial item and toasted hazelnut oil were not isolated.

A two-variant genetic proxy for potato liking was associated with insomnia, but did not measure potato intake, preparation or Parkinson insomnia severity. A cohort measured boiled or mashed potato and sleep duration with unclear direction. A completed pooled-preparation sleep-efficiency trial has no posted results.

A topical cinnamon patch improved the urgency item in overactive bladder, and high-dose oral cassia powder reduced voids in chemical cystitis mice. Daytime frequency was inconclusive in the patch trial. In a separate oral cinnamon rat study the bladder-distension response fell with cystitis and rose in controls. The dose, route and condition differences leave the direction of ground cinnamon for Parkinson urgency unresolved.

Nigella oil was studied in healthy mouse pellet-reaching learning, a task adjacent to dexterity; oil, healthy animals and unroasted preparation differ from toasted whole seed and Parkinson impairment.

The shiso rice trial measured odor pleasantness in healthy participants. In mice, induced anosmia blocked the forced-swim effect of inhaled isolated perillaldehyde. The inhibition of this behavioral response does not measure restoration of smell or an oral dried-shiso effect.

Parkinson diet menus include baked capsicum without a published apathy-item comparison. One dietary trial reports apathy scale changes with conflicting post-treatment comparisons and no identifiable roasted pepper exposure. Another trial gives baseline apathy without a published arm response. Isolated capsiate gave no identified willingness-to-invest-effort change. No direction for clinical apathy after roasted bell pepper is established.
A Parkinson case combined an oral multiherb formula containing Japanese pepper with intravenous levodopa for fecal impaction; neither ground Sichuan pepper nor dyskinesia was independently assessed.

Closest hand-function observations are one cervical-myelopathy case with a topical essential-oil blend carried in macadamia oil (grip 17.8 kg at week 1 to 27.3 kg at week 8; no fine-dexterity score) and one carpal-tunnel case with qualitative writing/coin-pickup/clothespin improvement during a blended topical protocol. Neither isolates macadamia oil or confirms cold pressing; no Parkinson dexterity estimate. The oral rat macadamia/soybean diet study measured fatty-acid pharmacodynamic markers, not hand function. No defensible direction for the claim. Open: find human Parkinson-specific pegboard/tapping/handwriting data or isolated macadamia exposure and verify preparation.

An injected sesame-oil rotigotine formulation changed peak and decay of drug exposure in rats. The search found no daily OFF-time estimate after eating toasted sesame oil in people with Parkinson disease.

The aqueous spearmint trial’s two doses pointed in different directions for depression-dejection, with baseline imbalance and an inconclusive overall comparison. The blended extract trial was inconclusive. Peppermint extract reduced mouse tail-suspension immobility alongside motor recovery. The sources leave fresh spearmint and Parkinson depressive symptoms unresolved.

Anxiety comparisons between oral macadamia and krill oils were inconclusive in military trainees. An unrelated topical study used oil in both arms. Neither identifies cold-pressed oral oil and a Parkinson-specific effect.
Canine kernel toxicity reports weakness and ataxia. Human macadamia oil experiments relate to acute fatigue and sleepiness. Neither measures Parkinson gait freezing after cold-pressed oil.

Observational PD subgroup of 13 participants with genetic variants shows plasma piperine versus total motor score r=-0.466, p=.108; pepper exposure source and dose are not verified, and no hand-specific dexterity score is reported. Total motor correlation cannot establish ground-pepper hand change.

Russian monograph reports intragastric alcoholic tarragon tinctures changed rat exploratory and search scores and describes sedation, without spontaneous sleep or insomnia measurement; dose form and species population differ from fresh culinary leaf Parkinson claim.

The Parkinson dietary abstract pools cauliflower and broccoli, and the likely overlapping drooling report gives no food-specific correlation. Conference originals use cauliflower as a shape description or a gastrointestinal diet trigger. There is no roasted cauliflower estimate for drooling.

Visual hallucinations after withdrawal of an injected drug and apparent visual behavior during historical topical poisoning occurred with active medicines in arachis oil. The reports give no cold-pressed grade, ingestion, isolated oil effect or Parkinson visual hallucination frequency.
Cinnamon appears in mixed Parkinson meal plans; MDS-UPDRS part II composite is reported without a separate handwriting comparison or isolated ground-cinnamon effect.

The resting-pressure juice crossover and separate raw-flesh and ambulatory studies give mixed or inconclusive results. A dementia case places watermelon in a visual error and measures positional blood pressure without an assigned exposure. A comparison measuring standing lightheadedness after raw watermelon in Parkinson disease remains open.

An oral peanut-oil control outside Parkinson tested strength and had no isolated oil contrast. The olfaction consensus mentions oil only as a potential topical vitamin A additive. Evidence does not provide a refined peanut oil pegboard or manual dexterity result.
Mixed caraway-containing meal provoked oral and respiratory allergy symptoms; seed grinding, culprit attribution and swallowing function are unverified.
The Thai Parkinson placebo used rice bran oil of unreported refining grade. The public motor outcomes are aggregate and give no handwriting subscore, letter size or disconnected oil effect.

No macadamia-oil dysphagia endpoint surfaced in dated catalog. Closest macadamia clinical symptom report is a whole-nut ice-cream allergy case with acute excessive drooling/anaphylaxis in a child, not a swallowing assessment or oil exposure. Oil-containing texture experiments evaluate rheology/softness of formulated foods, not patient dysphagia, aspiration or macadamia alone. No direction for cold-pressed macadamia oil and PD dysphagia. Open: search clinical swallowing studies and food texture formulas for macadamia oil; keep whole-nut allergy distinct from expressed oil.
2021 Parkinson randomized pilot used strained dried-leaf tea, with inconclusive motor UPDRS III total change p=.069; no separate facial-expression item or fresh leaf administration is available.

A randomized craniotomy study's supplement gives inconclusive patient anxiety VAS comparisons for ginger extract. Root powder results in healthy adults are inconclusive and the SSRI adjunct abstract conflicts with itself about direction. The Parkinson extract trial has no posted item results. Rat extract studies offer indirect behavior data. Grated ginger and clinical Parkinson anxiety remain unresolved.

A placebo trial gives inconclusive seated-pressure comparisons for a branded oil capsule. Regulatory surveillance reports hypotension for an ethanolic seed extract without event-specific counts or posture. The active comparator and earlier resting-pressure or rodent results do not establish cold-pressed oil and standing lightheadedness in Parkinson disease.

Apathy was lower after an uncontrolled cannabis extract delivered in olive oil. The oil grade is unspecified and no oil comparator was used. Parkinson diet-pattern surveys report favorable motivation in one cohort and inconclusive apathy in another. The refined-oil trial and Parkinson comparisons supply no separate oil-specific apathy estimate.

The five uncontrolled Tartarian buckwheat neuropathy cases describe dyskinesia without identifying the motor phenomenon or product in the accessible abstract. The biliary ultrasound patent uses the same word for gallbladder dysfunction. Common toasted groats and Parkinson involuntary movements remain unmeasured.
Whole dried celery extract improved some beam and grid outcomes in MPTP mice. The Parkinson mixed diet reports a motor total. These measurements give no fresh celery leaf effect on stride length.

A Parkinson registry plans a total scale that includes loss of interest after nanoemulsified seed oil. An unrelated blend registers motivation and mouse peel extract changes biomarkers. No aril-only intervention gives an apathy estimate.

A small essential-oil massage comparison reported defecation benefit but left methods and counts incompletely specified. The rosemary-extract trial has no posted results and tracks a combined bowel adverse-event question. The ground rosemary Parkinson constipation effect remains unresolved.

A methanolic dill aerial-parts extract inhibited rat ileum contractions in vitro. A sowa withdrawal study measured locomotion and rotarod performance. Neither experiment assessed neurological dystonia after ordinary dried dill weed.

The green-cardamom extract animal experiment measures drug-induced sleep. Acute and repeated black-cardamom extract reports share one registration and measure timed cognitive tasks with no daytime sleepiness scale. The results do not establish a daytime symptom direction after eating ground cardamom.
Topical allyl isothiocyanate in rats elicits swallows; a constituent applied to the swallowing apparatus is not eaten ground mustard seed or a patient dysphagia outcome.
2024 Parkinson trial saffron capsule versus placebo reported MDS-UPDRS III total interaction F=0.53, p=0.424; accessible report does not provide facial-expression item 3.2.

Fourteen diagnosed Parkinson participants completed three months of brewed green tea. Their mean Fatigue Severity Scale score rose from 28.4 to 32.1, and the same cohort's dissertation gives median scores of 27 and 30.5. This is one uncontrolled observation with no paired variance or exact fatigue p value. A postoperative brewed-tea trial favored less fatigue in a different clinical setting. Parkinson observational sources use ungraded tea, pooled domains or total caffeine and provide no comparable separate brewed-tea change. The exact exposure and outcome support a tentative worsening link. No controlled Parkinson fatigue estimate or recovered full body for the Jiang fly paper was verified.

One randomized 36-person older-adult meal crossover reports fewer six-hour post-meal spatial working-memory errors and better strategy after whole freeze-dried red raspberry powder versus control (NCT03879213, p<.05). A black-raspberry Alzheimer pilot measured global CDR without executive subscales, four-berry and multicomponent capsule trials do not isolate raspberry, and rodent studies are split between high-fat-diet benefit and Alzheimer-model null results. Acute meal testing, powder vs intact frozen fruit, and non-Parkinson population keep the lean against worsening at minimal_signal.

Cancer survivors reported less fatigue with kefir during exercise, but the journal and dissertation cohorts likely overlap, assignment was nonrandomized, the control received no matched drink and kefir flavor is unverified. A second oncology trial reports a favorable physical symptom aggregate without a tiredness item estimate. Kefir and water both improved acute recovery after exercise in adolescents. The exact preparation and Parkinson fatigue direction remain open.

A chocolate-matrix test found no clear increase in evoked saliva when some cocoa butter was replaced by hazelnut oil. A formulated gargle study measures wetting of excised tongue tissue. Neither supplies cold-pressed grade or a Parkinson drooling assessment.

Spearmint-flavored gum increased collected saliva during chewing in healthy volunteers. The two possibly overlapping reports disagree on peak timing. Faster swallowing during gum chewing in Parkinson is a separate pathway. Neither the gum studies nor the Sjögren spray registration measures drooling after eating dried spearmint.

One exploratory randomized trial in healthy adults reports favorable POMS 2 tension-anxiety change with boiled waxy barley versus rice, though final group medians were equal at 43, foods were visibly different, and eight participants were excluded (PMID39064742). Competing trials show a null cooked barley-flour versus rice-flour crossover (n=23), inconclusive DASS anxiety with multi-component talbinah, no anxiety scale when both arms ate barley (PMID40336123), and whole-diet NutriAct excluding gait-affecting Parkinson disease. Matching boiled preparation in the exploratory healthy-adult trial sustains only a minimal_signal against worsening.

Closest night-sleep lead is RRIPP-3, where macadamia-oil capsules were the active comparator to krill oil in trainees; no inert/no-oil group and no clear group differences in sleep-related measures, with no insomnia-severity endpoint. Separate 8 g macadamia-oil bread meals in healthy adults reduced acute postmeal sleepiness/fatigue versus controls in the same two-experiment family; this is daytime somnolence, not insomnia, and cold pressing is unverified. No direction for Parkinson insomnia. Open: verify original RRIPP-3 sleep tables/insomnia measurement and any Parkinson-specific insomnia outcomes attributable to oil.

Carrot juice served as comparator in an older-adult walking study and its usual gait-speed change was inconclusive. Purple carrot extracts affect other motor outcomes in rats. Provider and collection sources did not identify steamed carrot intake and a measured Parkinson stride length.

Topical ground clove and topical eugenol studies report dental pain relief. Ground clove powder in mice gave an inconclusive analgesia comparison. Isolated oral eugenol in a nerve injury model changed one thermal response but not mechanical responsiveness at observable depth. Neither result identifies a clinical direction for ingested ground clove and Parkinson pain.

A Parkinson menu offers green beans among many ingredients and gives aggregate motor scores. The original meal example and conference candidate supply no steamed-bean intake or individual facial-expression result.

Oral sweet basil extracts reduced motor impairment in mouse ischemia models, including inclined beam performance. Related publications vary occlusion duration and treatment timing. The human mixed diet gives a motor total without basil-specific stride length.

The small hot-sauce and mustard meal study tests a mixture. The separate cannabinol insomnia trial uses a paprika colorant in its formulation, with the comparison varying cannabinol. No study gives a ground-paprika comparison for Parkinson insomnia.
The Parkinson freezers/non-freezers study used clove as a smell-identification item; clove item comparison p=.212, without clove ingestion or intervention on gait freezing.

Cold-pressed hazelnut-oil samples show differing filbertone signals by kernel preparation. Parkinson-model studies of isolated filbertone report rodent motor-task and tissue findings. Human oral-oil studies provide other endpoints, leaving the cold-pressed oil effect on Parkinson resting tremor unresolved.
One Parkinson case reported longer medication ON time with cinnamon powder and honey. Both illustrated diaries mark 15 minutes of dyskinesia and give no severity rating or separate cinnamon effect.

A whole ketogenic diet improved self-reported voice handicap. The diet's oil ingredients were unspecified and intelligibility was unmeasured. Coconut food-frequency studies give broad Parkinson symptom composites, and a companion interview described talking. None isolates refined coconut oil or listener-rated intelligibility.

Painful-bladder surveys identified pineapple or juice as symptom triggers. A separate case-crossover fruit-or-juice flare result was inconclusive. A small survey lists pineapple separately but only pools incontinence impact. The larger urgency-incontinence study groups high-acid foods without a verified pineapple item. Raw pineapple and Parkinson urgency frequency remain unresolved.

The randomized Parkinson diet trial lists canola among low-fat plan ingredients and reports motor sums with speech items. No arm-level acoustic volume or isolated canola exposure is published. A primary oral olive-oil challenge used canola as diluent and recorded throat symptoms without measuring vocal intensity.

A synuclein mouse study reports forepaw stride variability of 15.76% with control diet and 10.18% with curcumin. Each diet contained the same amount of soybean oil. The Angelman-model experiment also held soybean oil constant between two blends. A separate ordinal stepping comparison uses spinal injury and provides no stride distance.

Parkinson menu and survey sources document cumin exposure options. They do not confirm toasting or a dyskinesia comparison. The Cuminum mouse extract and the different-species Nigella oral dyskinesia study use distinct exposures.

Oral extracts reduced immobility or improved selected stress behaviors in rodents. The feed study had inconclusive sucrose preference, and an earlier tincture report describes no forced-swim activity. These comparisons leave a clinical direction after dried culinary tarragon unresolved.

The prospective cohort pooled refined and pomace oil. The fully adjusted attention estimate was −0.006 z-score units per 10 g/day (95% CI −0.047 to 0.035), with an attenuated top-tertile comparison. A refined-oil trial gives an inconclusive 1-back activation interaction. Observational usual cooking-oil exposure and common olive-oil vehicles do not isolate a refined-oil attention effect in Parkinson disease.
Summer savory essential oil in lead-exposed rats measured rotarod balance rather than dystonia; oil differs from fresh culinary leaves.
Oat-containing animal and human interventions used combined products and tissue or global motor outcomes. Cooked oats and rigidity severity remain untested in the retrieved records.
Oral sage extract improved an index based on paw length and toe spread in mice. The result gives no stride-length estimate for ground sage in Parkinson disease.

A synbiotic protocol lists safflower oil in its placebo and has no posted bowel results. The Glut1 trial reported one constipation event in each blinded exposure period, and an oil-only pressure trial mentions bloating without a stool outcome. These comparisons do not give a direction for refined safflower oil and Parkinson constipation.

Inhaled sweet marjoram oil lowered resting pressure against air in nine healthy people. A later crossover in nurses did not confirm a comparable between-group effect. Standing lightheadedness after fresh-leaf ingestion in Parkinson remains unmeasured.
The severe-allergy citation identifies allspice. Clinical swallowing observations and ground preparation remain unverified. The inherited other-allspice dictionary match names a different plant.
Survey names anise in a mixed honey preparation and a separate broad sleep-disturbance category, without verified intake or dream-enactment frequency.

Closest PD human lead: a 2-week multi-food menu including unspecified pumpkin seed oil (with walnut, sesame and olive oils); 16 participants with PD, composite UPDRS III reported at follow-up, no oil-specific assignment/intake or separate handwriting/micrographia measure. Other nearby pumpkin-oil motor reports are animals and use non-micrographia outcomes (e.g., isolated compound stride or stress behavior); no defensible micrographia direction. Open: seek any primary human trial/task with writing size or oil-specific exposure, and verify any prospective result; cold-pressed preparation remains unsupported.

A historical article reports attempted hallucinogenic use without a verified case, exposure or visual effect. Parkinson dried-leaf tea reports a nonmotor total. Acute rat observations after concentrated extract do not measure hallucinations.

Parkinson cohorts used cinnamon as a diagnostic odor. A five-odor program including cinnamon improved a composite smell score after infection. Ground cinnamon in an oral diabetes study gave an inconclusive meal-smell contrast and the mixed oil registration has no posted smell results. The clinical effect of eating ground cinnamon on Parkinson olfactory dysfunction remains unresolved.

Basil appears in mixed Parkinson menus without confirmed dried intake or a food-specific apathy estimate. Inhaled basil oil reduced forced-swim immobility in stressed mice. This task did not measure clinical apathy.
No directly matched directional human Parkinson's evidence qualified. Local lexical pairs: 16. External records screened: 21.

Tarragon scent was one of many odors in a rotating mouse enrichment regimen; endpoint discrimination of two esters improved within enriched knockouts, but there was no isolated tarragon arm or consumption.

Dry-fried or raw huajiao volatile fractions reduced evoked mouse writhing relative to vehicle. The body and species voucher remain unverified. An uncontrolled mixed capsule improved oral discomfort, while a multicomponent IBS trial was inconclusive. Whole toasted pepper and clinical Parkinson pain remain unresolved.
The available saffron reports measure motor or mobility composites. Their gait and balance items can address some movement function but cannot give event counts for falls.

Whole macadamia kernels caused weakness with occasional stiffness in dogs. Rat oil exposure was studied for chemically induced tissue injury and cerebellar markers. No cold-pressed oil or Parkinson rigidity comparison is established.

Poison-center and high-intake reports describe unspecified tremor, intention tremor, myoclonus or seizure. Other original cases do not document tremor or a separate rest examination. Exact findings after ordinary ground-nutmeg intake in people with Parkinson disease remain unresolved.

The thyme-containing massage blend protocol registers facial anxiety in intensive care. Both groups in a Parkinson diet trial ate from thyme-containing menus and the trial reports a motor total without a facial-expression item or separate thyme effect.

Basil is listed in a mixed Parkinson diet with an improved motor total. Fresh preparation, actual intake and listener-rated speech intelligibility are unresolved. Rodent basil extract studies measure motor tasks without a speech outcome.

Closest endpoint match is two uncontrolled cases of benign essential blepharospasm (focal dystonia) using topical frankincense; cottonseed, almond or coconut oil may have been diluent, but the report does not map oil to person/outcome. The improvement described is attributable only to the mixed frankincense/botulinum history, not almond oil; no direction for cold-pressed almond oil. A rat 6-OHDA study used almond oil as carrier for CoQ10 plus atorvastatin and measured cardiovascular reflexes, not dystonia. Open: map diluent per case if full text/table permits and search independent almond-only dystonia exposure; oral/cold-pressed grade unverified.

BerryCare measured an eight-foot walk at baseline and documented fresh berry intake separately. Attrition prevented a before-and-after comparison. Rat plank performance concerns coordination, and no Parkinson walking-speed estimate followed raw blackberry intake.

The soup crossover found no clear difference in aroma liking, and the COVID-19 combination trial found no clear between-arm difference in combined smell and taste symptoms. Neither estimates olfactory impairment after consuming ground sumac in Parkinson disease.

Fatigue accompanied probable liver injury during concentrated laurel infusion use. A separate healthy-adult infusion trial asked about tolerability and a small extract study reported no adverse events, but neither gave a fatigue scale. The case concerns toxicity and gives no direction for ordinary ground-leaf exposure in Parkinson fatigue.

Canola oil is a comparator in a healthy older-adult ketone-ester pilot and a menu constituent in the Parkinson diet trial. The 2024 conference study that measured freezing is a separate anxiety and sleep protocol. Existing gait comparators did not count freezing events.

Topical sesame oil in knee osteoarthritis met a reported noninferiority comparison for an eight-meter walk. Oral sesame seeds with standard care produced a post-treatment Timed Up and Go difference. Several other routes involve injected or rectal oil. The 2024 congress item reports the same 15-person Parkinson cohort as the 2017 comparison. No study compared cold-pressed sesame oil consumed for Parkinson walking slowness.

An unofficial Methods transcription identifies sesame oil as a carrier for cannabidiol in an uncontrolled dystonia case series. The original abstract reports varied drug response and no oil-only arm. The sesamol animal result concerns catalepsy. Toasted sesame oil and clinical Parkinson dystonia remain unresolved.

Isolated anethole delayed a rotarod fall in toxin-exposed rats. The ground-anise trial reports general adverse symptoms without a fall count. A vitamin D protocol registers everyday falls, with aniseed ether among comparator excipients and no posted results.

Two human osteoarthritis trials provide measured stiffness readouts for topical sweet almond massage or placebo. Joint stiffness is different from Parkinson muscle rigidity, and the oral cold-pressed exposure remains unmatched.

A secondary summary of a Parkinson case describes worsening dyskinesia during suspected banana-associated levodopa wearing off. Laboratory tests found loss of levodopa when the drug was mixed directly into banana preparations. The case gives no verified preparation or severity measure.

The seed and mustard tea report tracked self-rated motor symptoms without counting falls. The compound trial list gives broad motor scales, with no posted results and no dedicated falls endpoint in the active trial. An observational cruciferous-vegetable result groups several foods. No comparison estimates fall frequency after steamed broccoli in Parkinson disease.
